entries.proposition: THE MYELIN DEFICIT IN THE NEURONAL DELETION IS LARGE AND IS CARRIED BY THE AUTHORS' OWN COUNTS: ABOUT THREE AND A THIRD TIMES FEWER MYELINATED AXONS IN THE CORPUS CALLOSUM AT P17. The paper's running text rounds this to 3.5-4-fold; its own Figure 5B averages give 180 to 55.

entries.proposition: THE CELLULAR SIGNATURE OF THE NEURONAL DELETION IS FEWER MATURE OLIGODENDROCYTES WITH MORE OPCs — A DIFFERENTIATION BLOCK READ OUT IN CELLS THAT NEVER LOST THE GENE. This is the signature an oligodendrocyte-intrinsic requirement would also produce, which is why the two cannot be told apart by the signature alone.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THIS PAPER CONTAINS A HETEROZYGOTE ARM WITH A GRADED, SUB-CLINICAL ELECTROPHYSIOLOGICAL PHENOTYPE, AND NOTHING IN THE CORPUS RECORDS IT. One Wwox allele is not silent in the neocortex: 17% of slices from heterozygous animals burst where no control slice does, against 86% in the homozygous conditional.
entries.snippet: In total, 0% S-Control slices showed bursting (0 of n = 11 slices across seven animals), 17% of slices from S-HT animals showed bursting (4 of n = 23 slices across 14 animals) and 86% of slices from S-KO animals showed bursting (36 of n = 42 slices across 24 animals).
entries.anchor: Results, neocortical hyperexcitability section, printed page 20 of 48, paragraph following the Figure 2 legend

page_anchor.crop_note: The Figure 2 legend on the facing printed page 19 states the same experiment with different denominators ('four slices from three S-HT animals showed bursting (~20%)'; '36 slices from 20 S-KO animals showed bursting (~84%)'), counting the animals in which bursting occurred rather than the animals assayed. The percentages differ from the running text's 17% and 86%; both pages were read.
